name: How to Choose an ADU Design Contractor for Different LA Jurisdictions

mainEntity.name: How do I choose an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County who understands both LA city and county-specific ADU zoning differences?
mainEntity.text: How do I choose an ADU design contractor in Los Angeles County who understands both LA city and county-specific ADU zoning differences?

acceptedAnswer.text: Los Angeles City and unincorporated Los Angeles County have overlapping but different ADU rules, so you want an ADU design contractor who can navigate both smoothly. Start by asking each contractor how many ADU permits they have obtained in the last 24 months in LA City versus unincorporated areas and specific cities like Pasadena, Burbank, or Glendale if relevant to you. Request permit numbers or addresses you can verify through local online permit portals. Ask them to explain, in simple terms, how ADU standards differ between jurisdictions for setbacks, maximum size, height limits, fire access, hillside rules, and parking. A qualified contractor should be able to outline these quickly and accurately. Review at least two approved plan sets they have designed in the same jurisdiction as your property to confirm they are used to local plan-check comments and corrections. Clarify whether they handle all communication with planning, building and safety, and any special agencies such as fire or public works. Finally, make sure their proposal clearly separates design, engineering, and permit coordination fees, and confirm how many rounds of plan-check corrections are included. This approach helps you filter out general contractors who “also do ADUs” from specialists who truly understand LA’s fragmented ADU regulations.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare ADU design contractors based on their experience with both Los Angeles City and unincorporated LA County projects, asking for recent permits in each jurisdiction, familiarity with differing setback, height, and parking rules, and examples of plans approved by both agencies. Verify they coordinate directly with each local planning and building department.
